title: Boolean logic in Ladder: a two-hand guard
summary: Draw AND, NOT and exclusive-or as contacts in series and in parallel, and enable a press only with both hands on the buttons and the guard closed.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real two-hand control or guard switch is built or wired.
objectives: Read series contacts as AND, a normally closed contact as NOT and two parallel paths as OR.
Build an exclusive-or (exactly one hand) from two parallel paths of two contacts each.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/TwoHandLd.ld.json three rungs are drawn: PressEnable, GuardLamp and OneHandWarning. The PressEnable rung checks the two hands but not the guard, so the press is enabled with the guard open. Make the press enabled only with both hands on the buttons and the guard closed.
stages.checkpoint: You can name the three conditions that must all be TRUE for PressEnable, and say whether they combine as AND or as OR.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict PressEnable at {{t:20}} ms (both hands, guard closed), at {{t:30}} ms (both hands, guard open) and OneHandWarning at {{t:40}} ms (one hand).
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TwoHandLd.PressEnable=true@20|ON}} at {{t:20}} ms; {{v:TwoHandLd.PressEnable=false@30|OFF}} at {{t:30}} ms, because the guard is open; {{v:TwoHandLd.OneHandWarning=true@40|ON}} at {{t:40}} ms, because only the right hand is on.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program enables the press without looking at the guard: PressEnable is ON at {{t:30}} ms although GuardClosed is FALSE. Change it so that PressEnable is ON only while LeftHand, RightHand and GuardClosed are all TRUE: ON at {{t:20}} ms, OFF at {{t:30}} ms. Leave the GuardLamp and OneHandWarning rungs as they are.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named TwoHandLd and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:50}} ms: with the guard open at {{t:30}} ms both hands no longer enable the press, and GuardLamp lights.
stages.checkpoint: PressEnable rises once at {{t:20}} ms and falls once at {{t:30}} ms; it is never ON while GuardLamp is ON.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Swap the series of the PressEnable rung for two parallel paths and see which assertion fails. Why is series AND and parallel OR?
stages.checkpoint: With the contacts in parallel, any one of them enables the press: one hand alone, or the guard alone, is enough, which is exactly what a two-hand control must prevent. Series needs every contact, so it is AND; parallel needs any path, so it is OR.

hints.text: Power reaches PressEnable only through contacts that are all closed. Which contact is missing from the rung?
Add a normally open contact in the first rung, to the right of RightHand, and name it GuardClosed. Leave the GuardLamp and OneHandWarning rungs as they are.

faultCases: The starting program enables the press without looking at the guard: PressEnable is ON at {{t:30}} ms although GuardClosed is FALSE.
